A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Vector-ICL research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching material that was relocated or merged.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on text, numerical regression, time series, graphs, and fMRI, including benchmark results and empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds cross-modal ICL comparisons and a synthetic time-series pretraining experiment.

M1.justification: Section 6.3 adds a synthetic time-series pretraining component that generates descriptions and QA pairs using regression, z-scores, and variability checks. The core architecture, objectives, and inference remain unchanged. Section 3.3's correction from training the LLM to training the projector resolves wording inconsistent with the freezing scheme already stated in v1.

E1.justification: V2 adds MoteStrain, TwoLeadECG, Wafer, PhalangesOutlinesCorrect, and Yoga as sources for synthetic time-series pretraining, including questions about trends, anomalies, and stability. This extends training coverage within an existing modality; the downstream benchmark suite is retained.

E2.justification: Figure 3 adds evaluated cross-modal few-shot ICL comparators for time-series classification, graph classification, fMRI decoding, and fMRI classification. This substantially expands the comparisons supporting non-text applications. Existing textual ICL, soft-prompt, tuned-encoder, and random baselines are retained.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a synthetic-pretraining transfer evaluation on the retained time-series classification tasks. It also specifies numeric-sequence inputs for the new time-series/fMRI ICL controls and textual graph descriptions for graph ICL. Existing benchmark metrics, stated splits, and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Section 6.3 and Figure 4c test whether synthetic time-series/text pairs enable useful projector pretraining and downstream transfer. Existing encoder-quality and numerical-embedding analyses remain. The fMRI category case study moves from Section 6.3/Figure 4c to Appendix A.2/Figure 5 without being removed.

E5.justification: Both versions describe Figure 3's uncertainty bands as 95% confidence intervals over aggregated configurations. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed disclosures, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: V2 substantially extends non-text results with four cross-modal ICL comparison curves and synthetic-pretraining results in Figure 4c. Existing plotted values also change: aggregate finetuned summarization at 20 shots rises approximately from 17.9 to 18.4 RougeL, and the fMRI-decoding horizontal reference falls from about 9.0 to 7.8. The text-result tables and matched appendix plots retain their results.

T1.justification: The encoder and projection definitions, Equations 1–3, and arithmetic-task formulation remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the added synthetic-data procedure introduces no new formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: lightweight projection enables continuous-vector ICL, pretraining establishes this capability, and task-specific finetuning improves performance across modalities. The additional experiments support this existing contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: V2 explains soft-prompt tuning as a control for lightweight adaptation, interprets numerical embedding blocks through shared digits and place-value structure, and argues that synthetic pairs address unavailable cross-modal training pairs. It also identifies instruction tuning's effect on vector understanding as an unexplored direction.

D1.justification: V2 documents synthetic-corpus construction and cross-modal baseline serialization, explicitly states that soft-prompt comparisons also receive up to 50 context examples, and changes the code-release statement from forthcoming to available. These disclosures do not establish rerunning existing experiments. Figure 4b's caption drops the earlier identification of Qwen2-7B as its illustrated projector.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Chung et al. (2024) and discusses Flan-T5's instruction-tuning benefits for few-shot learning. The remaining research positioning and cited works are retained; the widespread conversion to author-year citations is stylistic.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized method-prose corrections, adds a baseline explanation and acknowledgements, and replaces the main-text fMRI case-study slot with the synthetic-pretraining study while relocating fMRI analysis to the appendix. Most existing narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 gains baseline curves, a legend entry, and adjusted axes. Figure 4b gains numerical axis labels; Figure 4c presents the new time-series study, with its former fMRI panel relocated to Figure 5. V1 Tables 2–3 merge into v2 Table 2. Other diagrams and appendix result plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The added cross-modal ICL controls and synthetic-pretraining study strengthen evidence for the non-text applications, while training and comparison clarifications improve documentation. These are useful, bounded gains. Changes to some existing plotted values remain unexplained, and superiority is still not uniform across datasets: Table 2 reports 88.80 for finetuned Vector-ICL versus 93.24 for soft prompts on Rotten Tomatoes.
